react_result.final_narrative_text: The three independent pathway-enrichment paradigms — RaMP multi-database ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and Mummichog m/z-network activity — converge unambiguously on tryptophan metabolism (KEGG:hsa00380) as the dominant affected pathway. RaMP reports the KEGG canonical entry (map00380) as rank-1 with FDR = 1.08×10⁻¹⁵ and a 858-fold enrichment, with six of the eight input metabolites (L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, tryptamine, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, quinolinic acid) mapping to it; MetaboAnalystR independently confirms the identical KEGG human pathway (hsa00380) as its top hit (p = 1.79×10⁻⁷, 5 of 41 pathway compounds); and Mummichog scores its empirical-compound Tryptophan metabolism network as the global winner (p = 8.40×10⁻⁵, 13 of 14 metabolites, including near-complete coverage of the kynurenine-branch). The secondary winners — the IDO metabolic pathway (WP:WP5414, FDR = 6.5×10⁻⁹), NAD⁺ biosynthesis from tryptophan (WP:WP3645, FDR = 1.5×10⁻⁸), and the serotonin/melatonin biosynthesis Reactome module (R-HSA-209931, FDR = 1.4×10⁻⁸) — represent distinct functional branches downstream of the same trunk pathway. The six confirmed driver metabolites cover the full read-out of tryptophan catabolism: the direct precursor L-tryptophan itself, the decarboxylated trace-amine tryptamine, the classic neurotransmitter serotonin, its acetylated sleep-hormone derivative melatonin, and two consecutive intermediates of the kynurenine branch (3-hydroxyanthranilic acid and quinolinic acid, the latter being the direct quinolinate→NAD⁺ branch-point). L-Proline is a consistent secondary hit (arginine/proline metabolism, MUMM rank 3) but lacks cross-paradigm support at equivalent significance. Molybdenum, despite being an essential cofactor for xanthine oxidase, shows no membership in any high-ranking pathway from the three tools. The convergent evidence indicates that the treatment condition drives a systemic perturbation of tryptophan fate-sharing, simultaneously shunting flux through the indoleamine neurotransmitter arm (serotonin–melatonin) and the kynurenine–NAD⁺ arm, with likely implications for neuroimmune signalling and cellular redox metabolism.

  "narrative_text": "Three complementary pathway-enrichment tools converge on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant signal. RaMP-DB reports KEGG:map00380 \"Tryptophan metabolism\" as its top hit (FDR = 1.08×10⁻¹⁵), with six of the eight input metabolites mapped to this pathway. Across all three tools the confirmed driver metabolites are L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, tryptamine, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, and quinolinic acid. These six compounds span the full breadth of tryptophan catabolism, covering both the indoleamine neurotransmitter arm (tryptophan → tryptamine → serotonin → melatonin) and the kynurenine branch (tryptophan → 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid → quinolinic acid → NAD⁺). A secondary winner, WP:WP4210 \"Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD⁺ production\" (FDR = 6.01×10⁻¹¹), is supported by four of the driver metabolites and is consistent with the NAD⁺ biosynthetic context of the kynurenine arm. L-Proline appears as a secondary hit in the mummichog network (rank 3, p = 3.54×10⁻²), mapping to arginine and proline metabolism, but lacks cross-paradigm corroboration at equivalent significance. Molybdenum was not detected in any high-ranking pathway across the three tools. react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment tools converge on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant signal. RaMP-DB reports KEGG:map00380 "Tryptophan metabolism" as its top hit (FDR = 1.08×10⁻¹⁵), with six of the eight input metabolites mapped to this pathway. The same pathway surfaces as rank-1 in both the mummichog empirical-compound network (p = 8.40×10⁻⁵) and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (p = 1.79×10⁻⁷). Across all three tools the confirmed driver metabolites are L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, tryptamine, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, and quinolinic acid. These six compounds span the full breadth of tryptophan catabolism, covering both the indoleamine neurotransmitter arm (tryptophan → tryptamine → serotonin → melatonin) and the kynurenine branch (tryptophan → 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid → quinolinic acid → NAD⁺). A secondary winner, WP:WP4210 "Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD⁺ production" (FDR = 6.01×10⁻¹¹), is supported by four of the driver metabolites and is consistent with the NAD⁺ biosynthetic context of the kynurenine arm. L-Proline appears as a secondary hit in the mummichog network (rank 3, p = 3.54×10⁻²), mapping to arginine and proline metabolism, but lacks cross-paradigm corroboration at equivalent significance. Molybdenum was not detected in any high-ranking pathway across the three tools. The convergence across ORA (RaMP), KEGG PSEA (MetaboAnalystR), and m/z-direct networking (mummichog) provides robust multi-paradigm support for a treatment-driven perturbation of tryptophan fate-sharing.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis tools converge on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant perturbed pathway. RaMP-DB ORA (multi-database) identifies KEGG:map00380 "Tryptophan metabolism" as top-ranked with an FDR of 1.08×10⁻¹⁵, hitting six input metabolites: L-tryptophan, melatonin, serotonin, quinolinic acid, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, and tryptamine. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA confirms the same pathway (hsa00380) at rank 1 with a p-value of 1.79×10⁻⁷ and five overlapping metabolites. The m/z-direct mummichog algorithm also recovers "Tryptophan metabolism" as rank 1 on the empirical-compound network (p-value 8.40×10⁻⁵), with eight matched features spanning the L-tryptophan substrate through its serotonin, melatonin, and kynurenine-branch products. L-Proline maps as a secondary signal to the urea cycle/amino-group metabolism network in mummichog. KEGG:hsa00380 (map00380) is the cross-paradigm consensus winner with six driver metabolites from the tryptophan scaffold. Within this pathway, L-tryptophan is the initiating substrate; serotonin and melatonin occupy the neuroactive branch; 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid and quinolinic acid anchor the kynurenine arm, with 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid serving as substrate converted by KYNU (kynurenine 3-monooxygenase) to quinolinic acid, the NAD+ precursor. The treatment-group perturbation therefore targets the tryptophan catabolism network at multiple downstream arms rather than a single branch.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis tools converge on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant perturbed pathway. RaMP-DB ORA (multi-database) identifies KEGG:map00380 "Tryptophan metabolism" as top-ranked with an FDR of 1.08×10⁻¹⁵, hitting six input metabolites: L-tryptophan, melatonin, serotonin, quinolinic acid, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, and tryptamine. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA confirms the same pathway (hsa00380) at rank 1 with a p-value of 1.79×10⁻⁷ and five overlapping metabolites. The m/z-direct mummichog algorithm also recovers "Tryptophan metabolism" as rank 1 on the empirical-compound network (p-value 8.40×10⁻⁵), with eight matched features spanning the L-tryptophan substrate through its serotonin, melatonin, and kynurenine-branch products. L-Proline maps as a secondary signal to the urea cycle/amino-group metabolism network in mummichog. KEGG:hsa00380 (map00380) is the cross-paradigm consensus winner with six driver metabolites from the tryptophan scaffold. Within this pathway, L-tryptophan is the initiating substrate; serotonin and melatonin occupy the neuroactive branch; 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid and quinolinic acid anchor the kynurenine arm, with 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid serving as substrate converted by KYNU (kynurenine 3-monooxygenase) to quinolinic acid, the NAD+ precursor. The treatment-group perturbation therefore targets the tryptophan catabolism network at multiple downstream arms rather than a single branch.
